Sam / Ben —

Looping in a commercial sketch and a recommended accounting treatment. High-level: we propose a two-part construct — an Annual Anchor (A) + Monthly Surge-Absorber (S).

1) Annual Anchor (A):
- Customer commits to an annual token volume (Anchor A). We invoice monthly based on committed rate (blended per-token rate).
- Rebate ladder (annual true-up): if Annual Consumption C > A, rebate tiers trigger on the *next year* effective rate (i.e., growth incentive) or as a one-time annual credit applied to the final invoice for year. Example: A=100M tokens, if C=125M, apply 10% rebate on the incremental 25M tokens as a credit (sample math attached).

2) Surge-Absorber (S):
- Mechanic: pre-purchased monthly credit pool that's sized (S_month) as a percentage of monthly baseline. Credits are consumed before overage rates apply.
- Billing: S is billed monthly at a discounted reserved rate (lower than immediate overage) and replenished offtake-style. Unused credits at month-end roll into a short 2-month buffer before expiration (helps absorb short spikes).
- Alternative: fully reserved annual pool (if BluePeak prefers one CAPEX-like line item).

3) True-up cadence: we recommend annual true-up for anchor rebates + monthly reconciliation for surge pool consumption. A 30-day invoice window for disputes and a 60-day final settlement is standard.

4) Regional treatment: surge credits are region-bound by default (billing/legal), but can be configured to be transferable if BluePeak executes a cross-region addendum; that requires currency and tax pass-through and a slight premium on S (~5-8%).

Attachments: redwood-proposal-anchored-rebate-v2.pdf (narrative + worked examples). I've also added a link to sample calculations in HubSpot: HS-43921.

Notes for Ben/Karthik: pricing bands and sample %s are placeholders — we should finalize competitive tiering and rebate %s after pricing review.

Sam —

Quick legal/commerce clarifications:
- Rebate mechanics: we can do an annual credit applied as a single line on the year-end invoice (simplest) or amortize it pro rata across the first 12 invoices of the following year (requires language in SOW to support amortization). From ASC 606 perspective, we tag rebates as post-delivery credits — most enterprise accounting teams treat them as contra-revenue at the time of recognition; we can provide a sample treatment note for your accounting team.

- Region pooling: because BluePeak operates distinct legal entities per region, cross-entity transfer of credits requires either a master invoicing clause or separate intercompany recharge. If you want a single pooled experience, we recommend a cross-region addendum and a 5% surcharge to cover tax/compliance and FX exposure.

- Unused surge credits: default policy — non-refundable and expire after 2 months of rollover. Convertible option — at renewal, unused credits can be converted into a one-time discount on the committed rate up to a floor (we typically allow conversion up to 50% of leftover credit value).

Attached: pricing-examples.pdf (three sample annualized scenarios with numbers). Inline sample: Anchor A=120M tokens, monthly billed at $0.0022/token (committed blended). Surge S_month=10M tokens at $0.0015/token (prepaid). If monthly usage U=22M and baseline monthly anchor run-rate is 10M, the first 10M are covered by baseline, next 10M consumed by S_month, remaining 2M billed at overage tier ($0.0035/token). We'll put these in the proposal doc.

Will draft short clause language for the SOW and send before EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
